summary: AI task manager for coding with Cursor, Claude Code and other editors: turns a product spec into a task list your AI works through.

heroCommands.command: claude mcp add taskmaster-ai -- npx -y task-master-ai

sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: Task Master is a task management system for AI-driven development. You write a PRD (product requirements document), Task Master parses it into tasks with dependencies, and your AI assistant asks for the next task, implements it, expands complex ones and researches fresh information. It runs as an MCP server inside Cursor, Windsurf, VS Code, Claude Code or Q CLI, or as a command-line tool.
sixtySeconds.problem: AI coding assistants lose the plot on bigger projects. Task Master keeps a structured plan they can follow step by step.
whoFor: Developers building projects with Cursor or Claude Code
Solo builders using AI for whole features
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it for PRD-to-tasks parsing, a next-task workflow and support for many model providers, including Claude Code or Codex CLI without an API key.
requirements: At least one model: an API key (Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini, Perplexity, xAI, OpenRouter...) or Claude Code / Codex CLI

overview: The recommended setup is the MCP server: add task-master-ai to your editor's MCP config with your API keys (Claude Code users can run one claude mcp add command). Then ask the AI to initialize Task Master in your project.
Put a detailed PRD at .taskmaster/docs/prd.txt and ask the AI to parse it. Then ask things like 'What's the next task?' or 'Help me implement task 3'.
The CLI offers the same flow: task-master init, parse-prd, list, next, show and research. It is MIT with Commons Clause: you can use and build on it, but not sell it or host it as a service.

install.verificationNote: Commands come from Task Master's README. AIRepoHub hasn't run them yet.
prerequisites: A model API key or Claude Code/Codex CLI

steps.title: Add the MCP server
steps.code: claude mcp add taskmaster-ai -- npx -y task-master-ai

steps.title: Add API keys
steps.body: Put keys in your project's .env or the env section of the MCP config.

steps.title: Edit your MCP config
steps.body: Add a task-master-ai server that runs npx -y task-master-ai, with your API keys in env (for VS Code use the servers key and type stdio).

steps.title: Enable it (Cursor)
steps.body: Open Cursor Settings, MCP tab, and toggle task-master-ai on.

steps.title: Initialize
steps.body: In the AI chat, say: Initialize taskmaster-ai in my project.

firstRun.title: Write a PRD
firstRun.body: Save it at .taskmaster/docs/prd.txt; a template is in .taskmaster/templates.

firstRun.title: Parse it
firstRun.body: Ask: Can you parse my PRD?

tutorial.title: Turn a PRD into tasks from the CLI
tutorial.expected: A task list with dependencies and a suggested next task.
nextSteps: Set up the MCP server in your editor
